body:
I've added and reverted a commit with a benchmark scenario that tests how this PR may impact performance, as this code is part of the hot path.

You can run the benchmark with `node packages/algoliasearch-helper/bench/parseNumbers.js`.\
It runs 10 rounds of 100k iterations each, cycling through 1000 unique synthetic inputs per scenario.

I didn't measure any regression. In every single one of my benchmark scenarios, the standard deviation exceeds the absolute diff. This means the performance impact is within measurement noise.

🤖 **Disclaimer**: I reviewed the test data, but these scenarios were generated via a coding assistant.

***

Here are the results on my local machine:

I'm running 4 scenarios with 2 data sets: a "realistic" dataset, and one that tests edge cases specifically.
The scenarios are:

* Keys only: only root numeric keys (`page`, `hitsPerPage`, etc.) with no `geo` or refinements
* * geo: this adds `insideBoundingBox` with 1–2 geo rectangles
* * refinements: adds `numericRefinements` with nested `attribute`/`operator`/`value` structures
* Full mixed — all of the above combined

With realistic inputs (~90% numeric strings, ~5% non-numeric, ~5% already-numbers, <1% Infinity NaN):

| Scenario | Old (ops/s) | New (ops/s) | Diff (ops/s) | Std Dev | Relative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keys only | 1,352,134 | 1,315,951 | -36,183 | ±258,312 | -2.68% |
| + geo | 614,071 | 606,661 | -7,410 | ±45,826 | -1.21% |
| + refinements | 483,377 | 482,519 | -858 | ±30,848 | -0.18% |
| Full mixed | 363,175 | 357,719 | -5,456 | ±24,776 | -1.50% |

Uniform inputs (all value types equally weighted; the goal here is to stress-test edge-cases):

| Scenario | Old (ops/s) | New (ops/s) | Diff (ops/s) | Std Dev | Relative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keys only | 1,206,927 | 1,179,031 | -27,896 | ±65,422 | -2.31% |
| + geo | 575,140 | 574,114 | -1,025 | ±36,200 | -0.18% |
| + refinements | 485,707 | 470,192 | -15,515 | ±24,761 | -3.19% |
| Full mixed | 349,567 | 340,194 | -9,373 | ±18,532 | -2.68% |
